title: Oleshky truce ends after nearly 800 evacuated as Kyiv and Moscow trade claims over troop moves
dek: The six-day local ceasefire in Russian-held Oleshky ended on Sunday night. Ukraine's army says Russia used it to reinforce; Ukraine's ombudsman says no violations were found, and the Kremlin says no similar pauses are planned.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The six-day humanitarian ceasefire around Oleshky, a Russian-held town in Ukraine's Kherson region, ended at 10.59 pm Kyiv time on Sunday (2.29 am IST on Monday), after an evacuation that US First Lady Melania Trump, who helped broker it, said moved "nearly 800 people". Within hours, Ukraine's armed forces and its human rights ombudsman were giving different accounts of what Russian troops had done during the truce, and the Kremlin said no similar pauses were planned.

Ukraine's General Staff said on Monday that Russia had used the pause to rotate units, fortify positions and bring in ammunition, one report said. Ukraine's ombudsman, Dmytro Lubinets, who negotiated the truce with his Russian counterpart, said monitors had found no violations by either side, another report said.

## What happened

The local ceasefire began at 3 am Kyiv time on 27 October. Evacuees bound for Ukrainian-controlled territory were taken through Crimea and Russia, flown to Belarus and brought into Ukraine's Chernihiv region; other residents chose to go to Russia or to stay in Oleshky. Lubinets said on Telegram that the operation was "an important stage of joint humanitarian efforts" with Russia's human rights commissioner, Yana Lantratova, "coordinated by U.S. First Lady Melania Trump", one report said.

The exact number of evacuees has not been officially confirmed. Melania Trump said on X that the truce enabled "the evacuation of nearly 800 people". Ukraine's General Staff said its units had moved 167 civilians, including 22 children and 21 people with limited mobility, to safer parts of Kherson region. Lubinets said 105 pets had also been evacuated, and that the numbers for each destination could not be made public.

## Dispute over troop movements

One broadcaster aired drone footage, provided by a Ukrainian military unit, showing Russian armoured vehicles and soldiers moving through the town during the truce. Ukraine's General Staff said "the rotation of russian units, the fortification of positions" and increased deliveries of ammunition had been recorded, and that Russia "used the humanitarian pause to improve its positions", according to one report.

Lubinets disputed this at a press conference on Monday. He said the vehicles in the footage were marked with crosses and were used for demining under the agreement, which banned the movement of military equipment, and that one monitor from each side had checked compliance every two hours. "We verified that there had been no violations by either side," he said, according to another report.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov did not deny the General Staff's claim. He said Moscow could assume "with a high degree of certainty" that Ukraine's forces had also used the period to regroup, calling it common practice, and referred further questions to Russia's defence ministry, one report said.

## Will it happen again?

The two sides gave mixed signals. Peskov called Oleshky an exceptional case. "There are currently no similar plans, nor are there any similar initiatives at present," he told reporters, according to one report. But Lantratova said she and Lubinets would stay in contact, with the First Lady's mediation, about missions to Oleshky at least once a month, according to Russian state media as cited in another report. Lubinets said Ukraine was negotiating to resume deliveries to the town at least monthly, and that his office plans to set up a Center for the Return of Ukrainian Civilians, using Oleshky as a model for other occupied towns.

Melania Trump said she hoped Oleshky "serves as a foundation for lasting peace between both nations".

## The war goes on elsewhere

Fighting continued during and after the truce. Ukraine's military said Russia launched 193 drones overnight into Monday; its preliminary count said 154 were shot down or jammed. Ukraine's emergency service reported five people injured in Odesa region and, in a preliminary count, one person killed and 14 injured by Russian glide bombs in Izium. Ukraine has continued drone strikes on Russian oil facilities, and a fire was reported at an oil site in Samara region on Monday. Russia has not commented on the Ukrainian figures, and they could not be independently verified.

## Background

Oleshky lies on the left bank of the Dnipro, which has formed the front line in Kherson region since Ukraine retook Kherson city in November 2022. About 2,000 residents were left in the town before the evacuation, according to one report, against a pre-war population of about 24,000.

The Kremlin said in October that talks between the US, Russia and Ukraine were planned in the United Arab Emirates in November. India, which has called for dialogue and diplomacy to end the war, has close ties with the UAE and has bought large volumes of Russian oil since 2022, so any movement towards a settlement matters for its energy bills.
